title: ML systems
blurb: The frameworks and GPU kernels under deep learning, how large models are trained and served at low cost, and how recommendation and search systems evolved.

main.title: CMU 10-414/714: Deep Learning Systems
main.why: Automatic differentiation, layers, optimizers and GPU operations, each built from scratch into a small deep learning library. In English.

main.title: PyTorch 2: Faster Machine Learning Through Dynamic Python Bytecode Transformation and Graph Compilation
main.why: TorchDynamo pulls graphs out of ordinary Python by rewriting bytecode, and TorchInductor compiles them to Triton and C++.

background.title: PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library

main.title: Introducing Triton: Open-source GPU programming for neural networks
main.why: Kernels are written in Python over blocks of data, and the compiler handles coalescing, shared memory and scheduling inside each SM.
Computes attention tile by tile in on-chip SRAM, cutting the reads and writes to GPU memory that dominated its runtime.

background.title: Making Deep Learning Go Brrrr From First Principles

further.title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision

main.title: PyTorch Distributed: Experiences on Accelerating Data Parallel Training
main.why: Every GPU holds a full replica, and gradients are all-reduced in buckets while the backward pass is still running.

main.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
main.why: Each data-parallel worker keeps only a slice of the optimizer state, gradients and weights instead of a full copy.

main.title: The Ultra-Scale Playbook: Training LLMs on GPU Clusters
main.why: Data, tensor, context, pipeline and expert parallelism, and how to combine them, tested in over 4,000 runs on up to 512 GPUs.

main.title: MegaScale: Scaling Large Language Model Training to More Than 10,000 GPUs
main.why: Trains a 175B model on 12,288 GPUs at 55% MFU, evicting faulty machines and resuming from the latest checkpoint.
Stores the KV cache in fixed-size blocks like OS pages, so fragmentation no longer caps the batch size.

background.title: Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models

further.title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs

main.title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
main.why: A small model drafts several tokens and the large model verifies them in one pass, leaving the output unchanged.

main.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
main.why: Quantizes weights to 3 or 4 bits without retraining, enough to fit a 175B model on one GPU for generation.

main.title: DistServe: Disaggregating Prefill and Decoding for Goodput-optimized Large Language Model Serving
main.why: Prefill and decoding run on separate GPUs, so they stop interfering and each phase gets its own parallelism.

further.title: Taming Throughput-Latency Tradeoff in LLM Inference with Sarathi-Serve

main.title: DeepSeek-V3/R1 Inference System Overview
main.why: Experts spread across up to 144 GPUs to keep each expert's batch large, with prefill and decode on separate nodes.
One network narrows millions of videos to hundreds and a second ranks them, the two-stage funnel later systems extend.
Embedding tables are split across GPUs by model parallelism while the MLPs are replicated data parallel.
Billions of items pass through two-tower retrieval over ANN, a distilled first-stage ranker, a multi-task heavy ranker and final reranking.
Hand-aggregated sparse features give way to raw event sequences read by attention, with 2 to 4% more conversions on some segments.
Recasts recommendation as sequence transduction, and quality then grows as a power law of compute, as with LLMs.
Many retrieval sources become one LLM dual encoder, and per-post CPU ranking becomes a sequence transformer served on GPUs.

main.title: Embedding-based Retrieval in Facebook Search
main.why: Embedding retrieval added to a Boolean-matching search engine, with ANN served inside the existing inverted index.

main.title: The Faiss library
main.why: How vector search trades accuracy, speed and memory, through compression codecs, inverted-file indexes and graph indexes.
Scalar and product quantization cut index memory by over half, and SPANN is moving the indexes from RAM to SSD.
An LLM parses each query, LLM embeddings retrieve by exact GPU kNN, and a distilled 0.6B language model ranks the results.
